result:
Solution 2 matches my own derivation. Solutions 1 and 3 do not.

**Necessary condition.** The 2025 counts must be exactly 0 through 2024, so some gnome must see all 2024 others. That gnome must have all other gnomes inside one sector of width α. Take the regular 2025-gon. At every vertex the smallest sector containing all other vertices has angle 180·2023/2025. So α ≥ 180·2023/2025 is necessary.

**This bound is the right one for any placement.** In any placement, some convex hull vertex has interior angle at most 180(n−2)/n. At a hull vertex, all other points lie inside the interior angle. So for α ≥ 180·2023/2025, count 2024 is achievable in every placement. Count 0 is also achievable at a hull vertex, because the exterior gap there exceeds 180° and hence exceeds α.

**Sufficiency.** I did not prove that every α in [180·2023/2025, 180) works. Solution 2 asserts it, and I take it as plausible and as the intended result. This gives inf S = 180·2023/2025 and sup S = 180, so the sum is 180·4048/2025 = 16192/45.

**Solution 1.** Its "clustered configuration" argument is wrong. A cluster cannot make every gnome's gaps small. Every gnome on the hull of the configuration has a gap of more than 180°. So count 0 stays achievable and S is not empty. Reject.

**Solution 2.** Its answer is 16192/45, which agrees with the derivation above. Its sufficiency argument is hand-wavy but the result looks correct. Accept.

**Solution 3.** It is truncated, and its final answer of 2 is wrong. Reject.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
